name: How do design-build firms handle hidden conditions in older Los Angeles homes?

mainEntity.name: What happens when a design-build project uncovers rotten framing, outdated wiring, or foundation problems after demolition?
mainEntity.text: What happens when a design-build project uncovers rotten framing, outdated wiring, or foundation problems after demolition?

acceptedAnswer.text: Hidden conditions are common in older homes, especially in Los Angeles neighborhoods with older framing, past remodels, or deferred maintenance. Once demolition starts, a design-build team may uncover termite damage, unsafe wiring, slab issues, plumbing defects, or unauthorized alterations. The right response is to stop, document, and price the correction before continuing. Homeowners should ask in advance how the firm handles unknown conditions and whether the budget includes contingency. A good design-build team will anticipate these risks during preconstruction by inspecting access points, reviewing the home’s age and history, and coordinating with structural or trade specialists. The most important thing is transparency: the homeowner should know what was discovered, why it matters, and what options exist. Projects with older homes are much smoother when contingency funding and decision-making authority are established early.
acceptedAnswer.description: When hidden conditions are discovered, the contractor typically documents the issue, explains the added scope, and issues a change order or revised estimate. Older Los Angeles homes often reveal surprises after demolition, including structural, electrical, plumbing, or moisture damage. Good planning includes contingency for these risks.
